clue.text: Sailor, naughty fellow switching sides

indicators.note: L and R stand for left and right, the two sides, so those letters trade places in the word

parts.note: a rascal is a naughty or mischievous fellow

explanation.surface: A sailor is described as a rogue who keeps changing allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching sides' swaps L (left) and R (right) in RASCAL: its first R becomes L and its last L becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar is a sailor from India or Southeast Asia, historically serving on European ships.

clue.text: Allow a daughter to go to American institute

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone permits a daughter to enrol at an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to allow them in, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Records and clears after playing

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are played about with, giving a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone keeps records and tidies up after a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendars are records or registers of dates and events, such as a court calendar.

clue.text: Give new equipment to thief turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a looter is a thief who steals in a riot

explanation.surface: Someone re-equips a thief who has just appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses LOOTER, read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To retool is to fit a factory with fresh machinery, i.e. re-equip it.

clue.text: Deed to get party curtailed, fellows locked in

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: one word is shut inside the other like prisoners locked in a cell

parts.note: cut means shortened or curtailed
men are fellows

explanation.surface: A legal deed lets a party be cut short with its guests confined.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a legal document, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Fixed loose armband for actress

indicators.note: something fixed is put right, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress has her slipping armband repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is all three words 'loose armband for', fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora Robson was a celebrated English stage and screen actress, made a Dame in 1960.

clue.text: I am with master working with clay primarily, I?

definitions.text: I am with master working with clay primarily, I?

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the word clay is taken
the letters are set to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A speaker apprenticed to a master potter wonders what they themselves are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' shuffles I and MASTER to ERAMIST, after C (the first letter of 'clay', picked by 'primarily'); 'am with' joins them, and the whole clue describes such a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works with clay alongside a master is a potter, an artist in pottery.

clue.text: Put together, forsooth!

explanation.surface: An archaic exclamation is paired with joining things.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to join two people; and 'marry!' was an old oath meaning indeed, like forsooth.

clue.text: Clever Len devised part of message transmission system

indicators.note: devised means made up or contrived, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bright chap called Len invents a component for a communications network.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests telegraphy; the system is the body's nervous system.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron carries signals in the nervous system, which transmits the body's messages.

clue.text: Maybe watch an insignificant person

explanation.surface: A watch is set against a nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is literally a little timepiece, and a small-timer is a minor, unimportant operator.

clue.text: Ferry gold back repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the reversed pair occurs twice
back means the two letters are read in reverse

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A ferry carries gold back and forth again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses OR, and 'repeatedly' doubles the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off ferry for vehicles.

clue.text: Characters in protest and officers in deadlock

indicators.note: characters means letters, and the answer is a run of letters within the words

explanation.surface: Demonstrators and police reach an impasse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a deadlock where neither side will yield.

clue.text: The man getting married — month before is havoc!

indicators.note: before places the month ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: May is a month
he is the man

explanation.surface: A man weds after a month of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or chaos, a synonym.

clue.text: A fighting corps sent to a region

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A fighting unit is deployed to a region.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district.

clue.text: River roaring furiously, not half deep

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged
not half means only half of the word deep is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A river rushes loudly, though it is not very deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' shuffles ROARING to RIOGRAN; 'not half' keeps DE of 'deep'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is a major river forming part of the US-Mexico border.

clue.text: Old boys restored to health but not on view

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil; OBS is the plural
cured means restored to health

explanation.surface: Former pupils have recovered but are kept out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscured means hidden, so no longer visible.

clue.text: A French female embracing the German fellow? That's rare

indicators.note: embracing means the French word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: une is the French feminine for 'a'
der is German for 'the' (masculine)
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman hugging a German man is an uncommon sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' here is about cooking: meat that is barely cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare meat is lightly cooked, i.e. not cooked through.

clue.text: Fancy container with design for holding flower

indicators.note: holding means the first word keeps the second inside it

parts.note: a cachet is a distinctive mark or design, such as a stamp on an envelope
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: An ornamental vessel is designed to hold a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword's river (something that flows), not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache-pot is an ornamental holder used to hide a plain plant pot.

clue.text: Dish not English, also known as a Greek dish

indicators.note: not means the letter for English is left out of the word

parts.note: a mousse is a dish, sweet or savoury

explanation.surface: A dish that isn't English goes by another name as a Greek one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes E from MOUSSE, giving MOUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a baked Greek dish of aubergine and minced meat.

clue.text: Boring day for classes at Eton, say — double Latin

parts.note: U means upper-class, as at a public school like Eton

indicators.note: double means the letter appears twice

explanation.surface: A tedious school day at Eton with two Latin lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an exclusive English private school, so its pupils are 'U', upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull means tedious, uninteresting.

clue.text: Irritating conclusion to cause bad feeling

parts.note: off can mean annoying or unacceptable, as in 'that's a bit off'
the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: An annoying ending upsets people.
explanation.definitionFit: To give offence is to upset or insult, creating resentment.

clue.text: Declaim — before a church

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth in front of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to sermonise or hold forth publicly, as one declaims.

clue.text: Getting on a gee-gee outside home

indicators.note: outside means the horse letters go round the home word

parts.note: gee-gee is childish slang for a horse, abbreviated GG
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone mounts a horse outside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' is growing older, not climbing onto the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on means growing older, advancing in years.

clue.text: Gift of item of jewellery containing non-precious metal

indicators.note: containing means the joined words hold the metal inside them

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is an item of jewellery
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a base metal

explanation.surface: A present of jewellery made with cheap metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering is a gift or contribution, as at church.

clue.text: Relation wants bit changed at the front

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: A relative wants a piece altered at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed at the front' replaces the P of PIECE; the new N is not clued, so crossings confirm it. 'wants' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relation.

clue.text: One against one backing worker

indicators.note: backing means the second piece supports the first from behind

parts.note: a worker is a worker ant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One person opposes, with one worker in support.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is someone opposed, an opponent of a cause.

clue.text: No longer fashionable, port is ignored

parts.note: passé means out of date
Dover is an English Channel port

explanation.surface: An outdated port gets neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed over means overlooked, not chosen.

clue.text: Rise to be provider of eggs around breakfast time?

indicators.note: around means the hen goes round the time

parts.note: a hen lays eggs
eight o'clock is a typical breakfast time

explanation.surface: A hen gets up to lay around breakfast time.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to increase or grow, as tension may climb.

clue.text: Thought river must go to sea

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A river must flow into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Deemed means judged or considered, a past-tense synonym.
